% Problem Set 3 -- 10 problems. (The original PDF's header misprints "Problem Set 2".)
% Do not edit except to fix statement typos.
\problemset{3}{}

\problem{3}{1}{Give an example of a $T_1$ space where a sequence converges to more than one
point. Conclude that a $T_1$ space is not necessarily a Hausdorff space.}

\problem{3}{2}{Prove that the product topology $\T_{\mathrm{prod}}$ on $\R^n$ (where each
factor $\R$ is equipped with its standard Euclidean topology) coincides with the Euclidean
topology $\T_{\mathrm{Euc}}$ on $\R^n$ induced by the standard Euclidean metric.}

\problem{3}{3}{Let $\{X_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\Lambda}$ be a family of topological spaces, and
let $\phi\colon\Lambda\to\Lambda$ be a bijection. Prove that the product spaces
$X=\prod_{\alpha\in\Lambda}X_\alpha$ and $X_\phi=\prod_{\alpha\in\Lambda}X_{\phi(\alpha)}$,
both equipped with their respective product topologies, are homeomorphic.}

\problem{3}{4}{Let $\{X_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\Lambda}$ be a family of topological spaces, and
for each $\alpha\in\Lambda$, let $Y_\alpha\subseteq X_\alpha$ be equipped with the subspace
topology. Prove that the product topology on $Y=\prod_{\alpha\in\Lambda}Y_\alpha$ coincides
with the subspace topology on $Y$ induced by the product topology on
$X=\prod_{\alpha\in\Lambda}X_\alpha$.}

\problem{3}{5}{Let $\{X_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\Lambda}$ be an indexed collection of topological
spaces, and let $X=\prod_{\alpha\in\Lambda}X_\alpha$ be equipped with the product topology
$\T_{\mathrm{prod}}$. For any fixed index $\beta\in\Lambda$, consider the $\beta$-th
coordinate projection map
\[ p_\beta\colon\prod_{\alpha\in\Lambda}X_\alpha\longrightarrow X_\beta,\qquad
   p_\beta\bigl((x_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\Lambda}\bigr)=x_\beta. \]
Prove that $p_\beta$ is an open map. Is $p_\beta$ necessarily a closed map?}

\problem{3}{6}{Let $L$ be a line in the plane $\R^2$, and $\R_\ell$ be the lower limit
topology on $\R$. Discuss the topology $L$ inherits as a subspace of $\R_\ell\times\R$ and as
a subspace of $\R_\ell\times\R_\ell$.}

\problem{3}{7}{Compare (i) the ordered square $I_o^2$, (ii) the topology $I^2$ inherits as a
subspace of the product topology $\R^2$, and (iii) the product topology on $I\times I$.}

\problem{3}{8}{Let $X$ be a topological space, and
$\Delta=\{(x,x)\in X\times X\mid x\in X\}$ be the diagonal of $X\times X$, equipped with the
subspace topology inherited from the product topology on $X\times X$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
  \item Prove that $X$ is Hausdorff if and only if the diagonal $\Delta$ is a closed subset
        of $X\times X$.
  \item Prove that the diagonal map $d\colon X\to\Delta$ defined by $d(x)=(x,x)$ is a
        homeomorphism.
\end{enumerate}}

\problem{3}{9}{Let $X$ and $Y$ be topological spaces, and let $f,g\colon X\to Y$ be
continuous maps. Assume that $Y$ is a Hausdorff space. Prove the following statements:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
  \item The coincidence set $E=\{x\in X\mid f(x)=g(x)\}$ is closed in $X$.
  \item If $D$ is a dense subset of $X$ and $f|_D=g|_D$, then $f=g$ on all of $X$.
  \item The graph of $f$, defined as $\Gamma_f=\{(x,f(x))\in X\times Y\mid x\in X\}$, is
        closed in the product space $X\times Y$.
  \item Assume that $f\colon X\to Y$ is a continuous, open, and surjective map. Then the
        fiber relation set $R=\{(x_1,x_2)\in X\times X\mid f(x_1)=f(x_2)\}$ is closed in
        $X\times X$ if and only if $Y$ is Hausdorff.
\end{enumerate}}

\problem{3}{10}{Let $X$ be a topological space and $A\subset X$ be dense in $X$. Let $Y$ be a
Hausdorff space and $f\colon A\to Y$ be a continuous map. Show that if $f$ may be extended to
a continuous map $g\colon X\to Y$, then $g$ is uniquely determined by $f$.}
